name: Betty
description: An AI knowledge system for professional associations. Betty draws on an organization’s own content to help members and staff find answers, explore resources, and navigate services through conversation.
journey: A request to “put ChatGPT on our website” became an exploration of how an association’s own knowledge could support its members. That work grew into Betty, now a company with a team of its own in the Blue Cypress family.

name: Skip
description: An AI data analyst for associations. Skip lets teams ask business questions in plain language and explore interactive reports, connecting with existing systems to make data analysis more accessible.
journey: Skip grew into a product maintained and managed through the wider Blue Cypress organization.

name: Connecting people and knowledge
description: An experiment in finding useful connections between an organization’s content and the people who contribute to it.
approach: We used embedding models to represent content and contributors’ published work in a shared space. Those representations made it possible to suggest relevant reading, conference sessions, and people with related interests.
outcome: The approach was quick to implement, economical to run, and well received. It also opened up possibilities for matching reviewers and mentors—using primarily embeddings rather than larger generative language models.

name: A head start on conference planning
description: Helping a conference team make sense of a large collection of speaking proposals before the detailed planning begins.
approach: We combined clustering techniques with AI-assisted passes to group related proposals into an initial structure for sessions and tracks. The aim was to support a demanding volunteer-led process, giving reviewers something useful to refine.
outcome: The team reported meaningful savings in time and effort. The experiment provided a practical starting point while leaving the decisions about the final program with the people responsible for it.
